text.paragraph: Post-hospital visit for new atrial fibrillation, with thyroid tests showing hyperthyroidism. Concerns: New irregular heartbeat that began as unusual tiredness on a run; wants to know whether he can keep running; Wants to get back to a full working schedule and to exercise as soon as it is safe. [S]

Two tablets once daily; stop three days before radioactive iodine

tr.td: Transthoracic echocardiogram in hospital: normal chamber sizes, including the left atrium, normal valves, and left ventricular ejection fraction 60 percent
12-lead ECG at intake: sinus rhythm at 88 per minute, normal intervals, no ischemic change
Radioactive iodine (iodine-131, 15 mCi by mouth) for Graves' disease, with written radiation-safety instructions
14-day ambulatory ECG patch: sinus rhythm throughout, no atrial fibrillation or flutter, rare atrial ectopic beats
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes
Recombinant zoster vaccine, two-dose series completed

tr.td: Post-hospital visit for new atrial fibrillation, with thyroid tests showing hyperthyroidism
Two-week review on methimazole, with endocrinology consultation
Four-month review: levothyroxine titration and anticoagulation decision

Rate control with metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily; no antiarrhythmic drug or cardioversion while thyrotoxic, because most thyrotoxic atrial fibrillation reverts once thyroid levels are normal; taper the beta-blocker once he is no longer thyrotoxic

Stroke-risk and bleeding-risk scoring (CHA2DS2-VASc 1 for age 65 to 74; HAS-BLED 1 for age over 65) with a shared decision to continue apixaban 5 mg twice daily while thyrotoxic, then reassess once sustained sinus rhythm is confirmed after he is no longer thyrotoxic

Methimazole 20 mg daily after a baseline blood count and liver tests, with written advice to stop it and call at once for fever, sore throat, mouth ulcers, jaundice, or dark urine; stop three days before radioactive iodine
Endocrinology consultation to confirm Graves' disease, assess the eyes, and choose definitive treatment (radioactive iodine, long-term methimazole, or surgery)

After radioactive iodine: free T4 and total T3 within one to two months and then every four to six weeks until stable; levothyroxine once hypothyroid, started below full replacement; TSH four to eight weeks after each dose change, at six months once stable, then yearly; target TSH 0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L

Atrial fibrillation monitoring at every visit (heart rate and rhythm, blood pressure, weight, symptoms, activity, alcohol, tobacco), ECG when indicated, echocardiogram at diagnosis, CHA2DS2-VASc and HAS-BLED yearly, creatinine and blood count at baseline and yearly on apixaban, and sleep apnea screening at diagnosis and yearly
Return to running in steps once the heart rate is controlled, aiming for about 210 minutes a week of moderate to vigorous activity; limit alcohol to no more than one drink a day
Resting heart rate below 110 per minute without palpitations while thyrotoxic
Heart rate 72 in sinus rhythm on metoprolol two weeks after intake
No atrial fibrillation once no longer thyrotoxic, confirmed by ambulatory monitoring before the anticoagulation decision
Sinus rhythm throughout a 14-day ECG patch
TSH within 0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L on levothyroxine
TSH 6.4 on 75 mcg at the four-month review; 2.6 five weeks after the increase to 100 mcg
Back to running three miles several days a week without symptoms
Running three miles four days a week without palpitations
